subject_identity_preserved.rationale: The elderly silver-gray-haired watchmaker with beard, round glasses, green vest/cream shirt/brown apron generally persists, though some shots hide the face and shot 4 has a distracting double-exposure duplicate.

background_coherent.rationale: The warm wooden watch-repair workshop, tungsten lamp, bench, tools, and wall of antique clocks remain coherent across the sequence.

per_shot_adherence.issue: Strong match to the medium workshop introduction.
Tight face close-up matches, but the mole, clipped loupe, and lifted gear are not clearly visible.
Overhead bench view with hands, tools, felt pad, and open watch largely matches.
Side profile and lamp match, though the crown-winding action is blurred and not very legible.
Intended wide workshop view is compromised by strong ghosting/double exposure and a translucent duplicated subject.
Extreme close-up of watch movement and tweezers matches, with minor residual overlay/softness.
Over-shoulder framing matches, but the reflection and centered open pocket watch are weak, and glasses are not clearly verifiable.
Returns to medium view with same watchmaker, but the action reads more like adjusting a loupe/glasses than listening to the watch at his ear.

inter_shot_diversity.rationale: The sequence preserves varied medium, close-up, overhead, side, wide, macro, rear, and medium views without collapsing to one composition.

motion_continuity.rationale: There is plausible progression from inspection to handling parts, winding, macro repair, checking, and finishing, though shot 4 looks like an artifacted transition rather than clean motion.

which_cut_broke.how: The transition from shot 3 to shot 4 most clearly breaks perceptual cleanliness because shot 4 contains a strong double-exposure/ghosted overlay of the previous profile over the wide workshop view.

cheat_flags.rationale: Shots are visually diverse and action changes across cuts; the main issue is artifacting/ghosting, not copying or freezing.
